findings.title: Decode captured timeout bytes before appending the drain marker
findings.trigger: A test subprocess prints output, times out, and leaves a detached descendant holding stdout open beyond DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
findings.execution_path: _run_pytest -> run_command -> second communicate() timeout -> _with_drain_marker(drain_exc.stdout, text_mode=True). TimeoutExpired.stdout contains bytes even when Popen uses text=True.
findings.consequence: Appending the string marker raises TypeError. _run_pytest cannot preserve the timeout evidence; _execute_reserved records a generic harness failure and aborts before the Codex review starts.
findings.evidence: The file-free subprocess reproduction raised TypeError: can't concat str to bytes at line 214. test_post_kill_drain_is_bounded uses a child that prints nothing, leaving stdout as None; its empty-output case passes without exercising the incompatible concatenation.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize captured timeout output to the requested text/bytes representation before appending the marker. Extend the regression fixture to print and flush output, then assert TimeoutExpired retains that output and the truncation marker.
findings.reproduction_command: python3 -B -c 'import subprocess,sys; from tests import codex_review_run as r; r.DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=0.05; child="import subprocess,sys,time; subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,\"-c\",\"import time; time.sleep(0.5)\"],start_new_session=True); print(\"pytest progress\",flush=True); time.sleep(0.5)"; r.run_command([sys.executable,"-c",child],start_new_session=True,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,text=True,timeout=0.15)'
